Leave me alone. I'm too depressed to talk.
column2: 別煩我。我心情差到不想講話。

column1: I'm guessing it conceals the entrance to a secret lab.
column2: 我猜它後面藏著秘密實驗室的入口。

column1: And get some gnarly Egyptian curse?\255\003No way.
column2: 然後中個超猛的埃及詛咒？\255\003免談。

column1: Cool. The room clerk's a mummy.
I can't go through the fire.
I would, but not enough people are looking at me.
column2: 我是想啦，但看我的人不夠多。

column1: I suggest the national anthem should be^\255\003^`Bite the Demon Pancreas` by the Spewtones.
column2: 我建議國歌應該改成^\255\003^嘔吐音樂人樂團的 `咬爆惡魔胰臟`。

column1: N-n-no chance, b-b-boy.\255\003You have to p-p-put it in writing.
column2: 不-不-不行，小-小子。\255\003你得寫-寫成書面。
`制憲會議歡迎您提供意見^`\255\003`^批評^`

column1: `Stolen from the desk of GEORGE WASHINGTON`
Hey, keep your hands off of that.
It's going to be a famous log.
column2: 這會是根名留青史的木頭。

column1: It's big, it's heavy, it's wood.

column2: 別碰那個。\255\003那是政府財產。

column1: It looks like a martini shaker.
That's nice, but not right for a time capsule.
column2: 那不錯，但不適合放進時空膠囊。

column1: Please stop.\255\003You're making me quite drowsy.
column2: 拜託停下。\255\003你害我很想睡。

column1: I don't think he'll fall for that again!
I'm not going to give that to the father of our country.
column2: 我才不要把那個給國父。

column1: Stop reading that horrible book.\255\003It's hard enough to stay awake through this blasted meeting as it is.
column2: 別再唸那本可怕的書了。\255\003光是撐著不在這鬼會議上睡著就夠難了。

column1: I got something funny to show ya.
column2: 我有個好笑的東西給你看。

column1: It's lucky for you I'm so dignified.
column2: 算你好運，我這人有風度。

column1: Stop reading that book!\255\003I have enough trouble staying awake with Mr. Time Capsule here as my constant companion.
column2: 別再唸那本書了！\255\003光是身邊一直坐著時空膠囊先生，我就夠難保持清醒了。

column1: It's so c-c-cold in here that I'm afraid if I f-fall asleep I'll wake up as an ice c-cube in somebody's d-drink.
column2: 這裡冷-冷得要命，我怕一睡-睡著，醒來就變成別人杯子裡的冰-冰塊了。

column1: I don't think he'd be interested.
What he needs is a space heater.
I've got better things to do.
It's a little cage with a canary in it, perched above a little lever^\255\003Hmmm^
column2: 是個小籠子，裡面有隻金絲雀，棲在一根小拉桿上方^\255\003嗯^

column1: I guess I would have to start a fire to do that.
Someday, I'll let the bird have it.
column2: 總有一天我會讓那隻鳥好看。

column1: They don't seem to have gotten too far.
I don't think that's the right way to add an amendment.
column2: 我看那不是加修正案的正確方式。

column1: You can look, but don't touch.
Mr. President, may I offer you an excellent smoke?
column2: 總統先生，容我請您抽根好菸？

column1: Can you also provide me with a light?
Blast!\255\003I hate it when that happens!
column2: 該死！\255\003我最討厭這種事了！

column1: See if you can't find those for me, will you?\255\003There's a good lad.
column2: 你幫我找找看，好嗎？\255\003真是個好孩子。

column1: Very kind, but those are much too large for me.
column2: 你真好心，但那對我來說太大了。

column1: Strange^\255\003^I wonder if I should cut down on the coffee?
column2: 奇怪^\255\003^我是不是該少喝點咖啡？

column1: No thanks, I already have some false teeth.
column2: 不用了，我已經有假牙了。

column1: It looks pretty clear in here now.
column2: 這裡現在看起來清爽多了。

column1: Say, did you get the pen on our way out?
column2: 欸，我們出來的時候你有把筆拿走嗎？

column1: I found a blanket blocking the chimney.
column2: 我發現有條毯子塞住煙囪。

column1: Son, do you know anything about a blanket?
column2: 孩子，你知道毯子的事嗎？

column1: Uh, didn't the dude next to you have one earlier?
column2: 呃，你旁邊那位剛剛不是有一條嗎？

column1: Ah, you again.\255\003Listen, I'm afraid I'm quite busy.\255\003Affairs of the state and all that, I'm sure you understand.
column2: 啊，又是你。\255\003聽著，我恐怕很忙。\255\003國家大事之類的，你應該懂。

column1: You enunciate quite clearly for a man without his teeth.
column2: 以一個沒牙的人來說，你咬字算清楚了。

column1: I've been thinking about what you said about cherry trees.
column2: 我一直在想你說的櫻桃樹那件事。

column1: Is it true about you and the cherry tree?
column2: 你跟櫻桃樹那件事是真的嗎？

column1: I think it's freezing in here, don't you?
column2: 我覺得這裡冷死了，你不覺得嗎？

column1: Do you really have WOODEN teeth?
column2: 你真的有木頭做的牙齒？
哇，你就像喬治・華盛頓一樣！

column1: What are you looking at out there?
Now what are you looking at out there?
column2: 你現在又在看外面什麼？

column1: I've had a bit of practice.\255\003Martha frequently hides them from me as a joke.
column2: 我練過一點。\255\003瑪莎常把牙藏起來開我玩笑。
在思索偉大的真理啊？\255\003然後呢？

column1: Oh yes, it's quite true.\255\003Why, I've cut down ACRES of cherry trees in my day.
column2: 喔對，千真萬確。\255\003想當年我可是砍過好幾英畝的櫻桃樹。

column1: Cold?\255\003Why, you don't know the meaning of the word!\255\003I spent a winter at Valley Forge, now THAT was cold!\255\003Why, my spit would freeze before it hit the ground!
column2: 冷？\255\003哼，你根本不懂那個字的意思！\255\003我在福吉谷過了一整個冬天，那才叫冷！\255\003我吐的口水還沒落地就結冰了！

column1: Very much like him, according to my wife, MRS. Washington.
column2: 據我太太——華盛頓夫人——所說，非常像他。
